title: Create and send invoices from emails or job notes
summary: Paste job notes or a client email plus your rates and get a plain-text invoice draft with line items and a total. You check amounts, then paste into your invoicing tool.

tests.prompt:
Create a plain-text invoice draft from these job notes or emails.

Client: [CLIENT NAME], [EMAIL], [ADDRESS if known]
Job details: [PASTE EMAIL / NOTES / TIME LOG]
My rates: [HOURLY RATE and/or FIXED LINE ITEMS]
Expenses to include: [LIST or "none"]
Invoice number: [NUMBER]
Invoice date: [DATE]
Payment terms: [e.g. Due in 14 days; pay via [METHOD/LINK]]

Output a plain-text invoice with:
- Invoice number and date
- Bill-to block
- Line items: description, qty/hours, rate, line total
- Subtotal, expenses, total due
- Payment instructions

Rules: Only include amounts you can support from the notes and my rates. If hours or rates are unclear, list the ambiguous lines under "Needs review" instead of guessing.

setup.agent: Chat model for the draft; optional n8n/Make when job notes arrive by email
steps: Collect the job email/notes, your rate card, and the next invoice number.
Paste everything into the prompt and run it.
Paste the draft into QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Stripe, or a Google Doc template.
Send only after amounts and client details look right.
setup.approvalStep: Never auto-send. Verify hours, rates, and client address before the invoice goes out.
failureModes: Guessing hours when notes are vague
Missing expenses buried in the email thread
Wrong client entity or billing address

toolPicks.why: Email with a label → draft → your review folder.
toolPicks.whenNot: You invoice a few times a month by hand.

faq.a: Set the currency in your invoicing tool after you paste the draft.

faq.q: What if the notes are a mess?
faq.a: Summarize line items yourself first, then run the prompt. Ambiguous lines should land in Needs review, not in the total.
